text: Long-term-memory agents frequently reuse invalidated or obsolete memory and fail to reconcile evolving memory unless decay/refresh is first-class.
Agent memory should structurally separate evidence from inference (e.g. distinct networks for world facts vs. synthesized/derived beliefs).
Vector similarity is not knowledge relevance or identity; KG+vector hybrids outperform pure vector retrieval on reasoning, temporal and numerical facts, and expert rules.
Mem0 reports 91% lower p95 latency and >90% token-cost reduction vs. full-context on the LoCoMo benchmark.
fpf-memory is a vectorless, deterministic FPF spec runtime over 247 patterns and 13 routes; no vector DB, no remote indexing, no Python, no local LLM.
The fpf_memory client/endpoint name is a blocked legacy surface (May 2026 cost incident; review 2026-06-30); new memory tools must not reuse it.
FPF G.6 defines a typed, citable Evidence Graph & Provenance Ledger that makes admission/decision provenance addressable.
FPF A.7 Strict Distinction mandates separating Object, Description, and Carrier (and method vs. work, role vs. holder).
FPF B.3.4 Evidence Decay & Epistemic Debt treats evidence as perishable and makes refresh/deprecation explicit.
Embeddings / vector similarity should be the central organizing substrate of memory.
note: Rejected position retained to exercise contradiction handling; contradicted by claim:vector-not-identity.
